recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core follow-up is needed for FHIR-12062 unless a future Pharmacy work group decision revisits whether MedicationRequest.subject should remain mandatory.
issue_request: FHIR-12062 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution for Pharmacy. It asked to make patient mandatory in MedicationOrder, and the approved resolution was to change the element to 1:1 with guidance for an anonymized patient when the actual patient is not supplied.
initial_application: Git commit 4b93d6353b51eb1a8d46a63f1baec446f9a23115 explicitly applied GFTracker #12062 by changing MedicationRequest.patient from 0..1 to 1..1 and adding anonymized-patient guidance. MedicationOrder had already been renamed to MedicationRequest, and source/fhir.ini still carries the old-to-new path mapping.
additional_context: MedicationRequest is an active current-build resource. Later source refactors carried the rule into source/medicationrequest/structuredefinition-MedicationRequest.xml as MedicationRequest.subject. Later Pharmacy issues FHIR-39142 and FHIR-41408 clarified subject wording and Group-related medication references without making MedicationRequest.subject optional. Community searches found only the original tracker bot notification and no conflicting Confluence or Zulip decision.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current build-scoped StructureDefinition already has MedicationRequest.subject as 1..1 with Patient and Group targets and the approved anonymized-subject comment.
